epitaph: Max A. Million won the WICeW World Heavyweight Title in the fed's own first-ever battle royal on 4 October 1998, then lost it a month later to "Superstar" Steve Taylor, the second and last champion this capture records.
name: WICeW World Heavyweight Title
notes: The ledger's own two entries (4 Oct 1998, 8 Nov 1998) are both structured, each linked to its own dated show; no reign after Steve Taylor's own survives in this capture.

epitaph: Volcano won the WICeW European Title from Sean "Iceman" Stevens on 8 November 1998, an upset the broadcast called unpredictable; Kyle Barrows held it by the fed's own 10 December 1998 championship snapshot, the transition between the two unrecorded.
name: WICeW European Title
notes: The fed's own first-ever title match for this belt was billed for an unheld Thursday Night House Show after the 4 October 1998 card (Arch Angel vs. "Superstar" Steve Taylor); its own result is not recorded, and Sean "Iceman" Stevens's own path to holding the belt by 8 November is likewise unrecorded.

epitaph: DaLinkwent held the WICeW Internet Title through Black November before Blizzard won it by pinfall on 7 December 1998, ending a match Jupiter interfered in twice.
name: WICeW Internet Title
notes: How and when DaLinkwent first won the title does not survive in this capture; his own retention against Jupiter on 8 November 1998 is the earliest dated evidence of his reign.

epitaph: Berserk won the WICeW Extreme Title from "Mad Man" Max Marshall on 8 November 1998, then lost it to Down South Hustla in a Texas Death Cage rematch of styles less than a month later.
name: WICeW Extreme Title
notes: Max Marshall's own prior reign as this title's holder is referenced only in prose, with no dated ledger surviving for it in this capture.

epitaph: Red Dogg won the WICeW Television Title from Gangsta New Jack on 5 December 1998, then successfully defended it against Junior Skaggs one week later.
name: WICeW Television Title
notes: Gangsta New Jack's own prior reign, defended in an 8 November 1998 ladder match against Scorpion, is not entered as its own reign row -- no dated ledger survives for when he first won it.

epitaph: Gangsta New Jack won the fed's own first WICeW Cruiserweight Title in a ten-man battle royal on 4 October 1998; Blizzard held it by the 10 December 1998 championship snapshot, the transition unrecorded.
name: WICeW Cruiserweight Title
notes: An 8 November 1998 card billed a "Cruiserweight Title match" between Kyle Barrows and Blizzard (a two-out-of-three-falls draw) while Gangsta New Jack was still the attested champion -- recorded as billed on that show, not reconciled into this ledger.

epitaph: The Demon Knights already held the WICeW World Tag Team Title when this capture's own record opens, retaining it via disqualification on 4 October 1998; Original Gangstaz held it by the 10 December 1998 championship snapshot, the transition unrecorded.
name: WICeW World Tag Team Title
notes: Original Gangstaz is billed defeating Nuclear Disaster the same night as the 10 December 1998 snapshot, but no card in this capture shows the Demon Knights actually losing the belt.

epitaph: The Hickerson Brothers won the fed's own first WICeW North American Tag Team Title on 4 October 1998 and held it through a loser-leaves-WICeW defense a month later, before President Gregory Joseph stripped them of it on 12 December 1998.
name: WICeW North American Tag Team Title
notes: President Joseph announced the vacant title would be filled at the fed's next pay-per-view, not itself captured in this holding.

epitaph: Masta Gangsta was named the fed's own first WICeW United States Heavyweight Champion as runner-up of the 4 October 1998 World Heavyweight Title battle royal; TRU held the belt by 8 November 1998, and it sat vacant by the 10 December 1998 championship snapshot.
name: WICeW United States Heavyweight Title
notes: How and when TRU won the title from Masta Gangsta is not recorded; TRU's own bio card lists the title with no date, and his own successful defense against Sabre on 8 November 1998 is the only dated corroboration on file. How and when the belt went vacant by 10 December is likewise unrecorded.
